questions.question: Which of the following is used to receive and send computer files over telephone lines?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is used to receive and send computer files over telephone lines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Modem.

 Key Points

  • A Modem (Modulator-Demodulator) is a hardware component that allows a computer or another device, such as a router or switch, to connect to the Internet.
  • It converts or "modulates" an analog signal from a telephone or cable wire to digital data (1s and 0s) that a computer can recognize.
  • It can also convert digital data from a computer or other device into an analog signal that can be sent over standard telephone lines.

 Additional Information

  • Modems are not needed for fiber optic connections because the signals are transmitted digitally from beginning to end.

questions.question: What does HLL stand for in computing?
questions.questionHtml: What does HLL stand for in computing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is High-Level Language.

Key Points

  • Computer programming languages are broadly categorized into 2 types namely – High-Level Language and Low-Level Language.
  • The abbreviation for High-Level Language is HLL and Low-Level Language is LLL.
  • A high-level language (HLL) is a programming language such as C, FORTRAN, or Pascal that enables a programmer to write programs that are more or less independent of a particular type of computer.
  • Such languages are considered high-level because they are closer to human languages and further from machine languages.

​Important Points

  • Lisp, Prolog, Python, and R are the main AI programming languages that are best suited for development and design for different kinds of software.
  • C language is developed by Dennis M. Ritchie in the early 1970s.
  • Father of Computer - Charles Babbage
  • Mother of Computer - Ada Lovelace
  • The first computer programming language was created in 1883 by Ada Lovelace.

questions.question: Which of the following is the full form of ASCII?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the full form of ASCII?

options.text: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
options.html: American Standard Code for Information Interchange

options.text: Analytical Scientific Code for Information Interchange
options.html: Analytical Scientific Code for Information Interchange

options.text: Asian Standard Code for Information Interchange
options.html: Asian Standard Code for Information Interchange

options.text: Analytical Standard Code for Intermitted Information
options.html: Analytical Standard Code for Intermitted Information

questions.solution:
The correct answer is American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

Key Points

  • ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.
  • It's a standard data-transmission code used by smaller and less powerful computers to represent textual data (letters, numbers, and punctuation marks) as well as non-input-device commands (control characters).
  • Like other coding systems, it turns data into standardised digital formats that let computers communicate with one another and process and store data more efficiently.
  • The ASCII code was created for teletypewriters but has now found widespread use in personal computers.
  • Seven-digit binary integers, or numbers made up of multiple sequences of 0s and 1s, are used in the standard ASCII coding.
  • Because there are 128 different possible combinations of seven 0s and 1s, the code can represent 128 different characters.
  • A lowercase "p" is represented by the binary sequence 1110000, while an uppercase "P" is represented by the binary sequence 1010000.
  • The seven information bits plus a parity bit (used for error-checking purposes or to represent special symbols) in ASCII code are usually placed in an eight-bit field.

questions.question: ______ is an advanced discipline that teaches students how to analyse and find patterns in large amounts of data.
questions.questionHtml: ______ is an advanced discipline that teaches students how to analyse and find patterns in large amounts of data.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Data Science.

Key Points

  • Data science is an advanced discipline that teaches students how to analyze and find patterns in large amounts of data.
    • Data science is a process in which the goal is to make better choices.
    • To make better choices, data should be collected to properly analyze the situation.
    • Once the situation has been analyzed, then data scientists can make decisions to improve various outcomes.
    • Data science is a field of applied mathematics and statistics that provides useful information based on large amounts of complex data or big data.
    • Data science, or data-driven science, combines aspects of different fields with the aid of computation to interpret reams of data for decision-making purposes.

Additional Information

  • Computer science is the study of computers and computing as well as their theoretical and practical applications.
    • Computer science applies the principles of mathematics, engineering, and logic to a plethora of functions, including algorithm formulation, software, and hardware development, and artificial intelligence.
  • Computer programming is the process of performing a particular computation (or more generally, accomplishing a specific computing result), usually by designing/building an executable computer program.
    • Programming involves tasks such as analysis, generating algorithms, profiling algorithms' accuracy and resource consumption, and the implementation of algorithms (usually in a chosen programming language, commonly referred to as coding).
  • Software development is the process of conceiving, specifying, designing, programming, documenting, testing, and bug fixing involved in creating and maintaining applications, frameworks, or other software components.
    • Software development involves writing and maintaining the source code but in a broader sense.
    • It includes all processes from the conception of the desired software through to the final manifestation of the software, typically in a planned and structured process.
    • Software development also includes research, new development, prototyping, modification, reuse, re-engineering, maintenance, or any other activities that result in software products.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique identifier for each user, typically in the format of name@domain.com?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a unique identifier for each user, typically in the format of name@domain.com?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 3) Email address.

Key Points

  • An email address is a unique identifier for each user, typically in the format of name@domain.com.
  • Email addresses are used to send and receive electronic messages over the internet.
  • They consist of two main parts: the local part (before the @ symbol) and the domain part (after the @ symbol).
  • The domain part usually represents the email service provider, such as gmail.com or yahoo.com.
  • Each email address must be unique to ensure that messages are delivered to the correct recipient.

Additional Information

  • Local Part
    • The local part of an email address can include letters, numbers, and certain special characters such as periods, underscores, and hyphens.
    • It is case-insensitive, meaning user@example.com and User@Example.com are considered the same.
  • Domain Part
    • The domain part follows the @ symbol and typically represents the email service provider's domain name.
    • Common domains include gmail.com, yahoo.com, and outlook.com.
    • It can also include custom domains, such as yourcompany.com.
  • Email Protocols
    • SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails.
    • IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) and POP3 (Post Office Protocol) are used to retrieve emails from a server.
  • Email Clients
    • Email clients are software applications used to access and manage a user's email. Examples include Microsoft Outlook, Mozilla Thunderbird, and Apple Mail.

questions.question: Which of the following is the shortcut key to Paste text in MS Word 365?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the shortcut key to Paste text in MS Word 365?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is Ctrl + V.

Key Points

  • The shortcut key Ctrl + V is universally used to paste text or other content in various applications, including MS Word 365.
  • It is part of the standard set of keyboard shortcuts developed by Microsoft Windows and adopted by other operating systems for basic functions like copy, cut, and paste.
  • When a user copies or cuts content, it is stored in the clipboard. Using Ctrl + V, the content from the clipboard can be pasted at the cursor's location.
  • This shortcut enhances productivity by eliminating the need for manual pasting through the context menu or toolbar.
  • Ctrl + V works across different versions of MS Word, including Office 365, 2019, 2016, 2013, 2010, and earlier versions.
  • Users who rely on keyboard shortcuts for efficiency find Ctrl + V indispensable for editing and formatting tasks.

Additional Information

  • Ctrl + Shift + V
    • The shortcut key Ctrl + Shift + V is used in certain applications (such as Google Docs or web applications) to paste text without formatting.
    • However, this functionality is not available in MS Word 365.
    • In MS Word, pasting without formatting can be done manually via the "Paste Special" option in the ribbon.
  • Shift + V
    • Shift + V is not a valid shortcut for pasting text in MS Word 365 or any other version of MS Word.
    • This shortcut has no assigned function related to pasting content in Microsoft Office applications.
  • Ctrl + C
    • Ctrl + C is the shortcut key used to copy content to the clipboard in MS Word and other applications.
    • This function works in tandem with Ctrl + V, as content must first be copied or cut before it can be pasted.

questions.question: Which of the following is a pointing device used to move an object on the screen of a computer in any direction?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is a pointing device used to move an object on the screen of a computer in any direction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Joystick.

Key Points

  • A joystick is an input device consisting of a stick that pivots on a base and reports its angle or direction to the device it is controlling.
  • A joystick, also known as the control column, is the principal control device in the cockpit of many civilian and military aircraft, either as a center stick or side-stick. It often has supplementary switches to control various aspects of the aircraft's flight.
  • Joysticks are often used to control video games, and usually have one or more push-buttons whose state can also be read by the computer.
  • A popular variation of the joystick used on modern video game consoles is the analog stick. Joysticks are also used for controlling machines such as cranes, trucks, underwater unmanned vehicles, wheelchairs, surveillance cameras, and zero-turning radius lawnmowers. 

Additional Information

  • Server
    • ​A server is a computer or system that provides resources, data, services, or programs to other computers, known as clients, over a network.
    • In theory, whenever computers share resources with client machines they are considered servers.
    • There are many types of servers, including web servers, mail servers, and virtual servers.
  • Modem
    • A modulator-demodulator, or simply a modem, is a hardware device that converts data from a digital format, intended for communication directly between devices with specialized wiring, into one suitable for a transmission medium such as telephone lines or radio.
    • A modem modulates one or more carrier wave signals to encode digital information for transmission and demodulates signals to decode the transmitted information. The goal is to produce a signal that can be transmitted easily and decoded reliably to reproduce the original digital data.

questions.question: Which of the following operating systems guarantees a response within specified time constraints?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following operating systems guarantees a response within specified time constraints?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a Real-time Operating system.

Key Points

  •  Real-time operating system
    • Real-time operating systems are used in environments where a large number of events, mostly external to the computer system, must be accepted and processed in a short time within certain deadlines.
    • The processing in this type of system must occur within the specified constraints.
    • Examples of the real-time operating systems: Airline traffic control systems, Command Control Systems, Airlines reservation system, Heart Peacemaker, Network Multimedia Systems, Robot, etc.

Additional Information

  •  Distributed operating system
    • A distributed operating system is an essential type of operating system. 
    • They use many central processors to serve multiple real-time applications and users.
    • It connects multiple computers via a single communication channel.
    • They are also known as loosely coupled systems.
  • Time-sharing operating system
    • A time-sharing operating system allows multiple users to share computers simultaneously.
    • A time-sharing operating system uses CPU scheduling and multi-programming to provide each with a small portion of a shared computer at once.
    • Examples of time Sharing are Multics, Unix.
  • ​​Interactive operating system
    • An interactive operating system is one that allows the user to directly interact with the operating system whilst one or more programs are running.
    • Both the UNIX operating system and DOS (Disk Operating System) are classic examples.

options.html: ‘Save’ is used to save file in a local computer, while ‘Save As’ is used to save it on cloud.

options.html: ‘Save’ is used to save file as read only file, while ‘Save As’ is used to save it as editable file.

options.text: ‘Save’ is used to save the document for the first time, while ‘Save As’ is used to save the document with a new name or different file format.
options.html: ‘Save’ is used to save the document for the first time, while ‘Save As’ is used to save the document with a new name or different file format.

options.html: ‘Save’ is used to save file in compressed manner, while ‘Save As’ is used to save it as it is.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ‘Save’ is used to save the document for the first time, while ‘Save As’ is used to save the document with a new name or different file format.

Key Points

  • Save:
    • This command updates the existing file with the current changes. It overwrites the previous version of the file, effectively replacing it with the latest modifications. This is typically used for ongoing work on a document, where you want to preserve the most recent changes to the same file.
  • Save As:
    • This command creates a new copy of the file, allowing you to save it under a different name or in a different location. This preserves the original file intact while creating a separate version of the document. This is useful when you want to:
  • Create a backup: Save a copy of the file for safekeeping.
  • Save different versions: Maintain multiple versions of the document with different modifications.
  • Change the file format: Save the document in a different format (e.g., PDF, RTF, or DOCX).
  • Save the file in a different location: Move the file to a different folder or drive.
  • In essence:
    • Save: Updates the existing file.
    • Save As: Creates a new copy of the file.

  • Users can adjust the font size to enhance the importance of certain sections of the text or to fit more text on a page.

Additional Information

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct combination of a column letter and a row number that identifies a cell on a worksheet in MS Excel?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the correct combination of a column letter and a row number that identifies a cell on a worksheet in MS Excel?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A3.

Key Points

  • In MS Excel, cells are identified by a combination of column letters and row numbers.
  • Columns in Excel are labeled with letters, starting from A, B, C, and so on.
  • Rows in Excel are labeled with numbers, starting from 1, 2, 3, and so on.
  • A cell reference combines a column letter with a row number to uniquely identify a cell, such as A3.

Additional Information

  • Cell Reference:
    • A cell reference in Excel refers to the cell or a range of cells on a worksheet and can be used in formulas to access the values or data contained within those cells.
    • For example, the cell reference A3 refers to the cell at the intersection of column A and row 3.
  • Column Letters:
    • Columns in Excel are denoted by letters, starting from A to Z, then AA, AB, and so on.
    • Each column letter uniquely identifies a vertical group of cells in the worksheet.
  • Row Numbers:
    • Rows in Excel are denoted by numbers, starting from 1 and increasing sequentially.
    • Each row number uniquely identifies a horizontal group of cells in the worksheet.
  • Cell Address:
    • The cell address is a combination of the column letter and the row number and uniquely identifies a cell on the worksheet.
    • For example, in the cell address A3, 'A' is the column letter and '3' is the row number.

questions.question: What do you mean by LAN?
questions.questionHtml: What do you mean by LAN?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Local Area Network.

Key Points

  • A Local Area Network (LAN) is a network that connects computers within a limited area such as a residence, school, laboratory, university campus or office building.
  • LANs are characterized by higher data-transfer rates, smaller geographic range, and lack of a need for leased telecommunication lines.
  • They are typically used to share resources such as files, printers, games, or other applications.
  • LANs can be wired (using Ethernet cables) or wireless (using Wi-Fi).

Additional Information

  • Wide Area Network (WAN)
    • A WAN spans a large geographic area such as a state, province, or country.
    • WANs often connect multiple smaller networks, such as LANs or MANs.
    • The most well-known example of a WAN is the Internet.
    • WANs are typically established using leased telecommunication lines.
  • Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)
    • A MAN spans a larger area than a LAN but smaller than a WAN, such as a city or a large campus.
    • MANs are designed to extend over an entire city, and they may be used to connect several LANs within a city.
    • MANs are typically owned by a single organization such as a government entity or large corporation.
  • Personal Area Network (PAN)
    • A PAN is a computer network organized around an individual person within a single building.
    • PANs are used to connect personal devices such as computers, smartphones, tablets, printers, and other devices.
    • Bluetooth and USB are common technologies used to create PANs.

questions.question: Which of the following options is used while printing documents in MS Word 365, i.e. if we want to print all the pages from 7 till 10, then the printer should print only the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th pages?
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following options is used while printing documents in MS
Word 365, i.e. if we want to print all the pages from 7 till 10, then the printer should print only the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th pages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Print Custom Range.

Key Points

  • Print Custom Range:
    • This setting allows you to specify the exact pages you want to print within your document.
    • Instead of printing the entire document, you can select a specific range of pages.
    • For example, to print pages 7 through 10, you would enter "7-10" in the "Pages" field of the Print dialog box.
    • This is useful when you only need specific sections or portions of your document.

Additional Information

  • Print One-Sided:
    • This option ensures that each page is printed on only one side of the paper.
    • It's the default setting for most printing jobs.
    • This option is particularly useful when printing on single sheets of paper or if your printer doesn't support double-sided printing.
  • Collated:
    • When printing multiple copies of a document, the "Collated" option arranges the pages in the correct order for each copy.
    • For example, if you're printing two copies of a four-page document, collated printing will produce two sets of pages 1-4, rather than printing all copies of page 1, then all copies of page 2, and so on.
  • Orientation:
    • This setting determines the page layout:
    • Portrait: The page is taller than it is wide (the standard orientation for most documents).
    • Landscape: The page is wider than it is tall (suitable for wide tables, charts, or images).
    • You can choose the orientation that best suits the content of your document.
